issue.body: Part of #1065 (the Rust SDK slice; the issue stays open for the second SDK and the component-model/WIT decision, both Drew-owned per the triage on the issue). Queue task 13926. ## What this adds **`pkgs/id/examples/rust-world` — `plaza-sdk`, the Rust guest SDK.** A pure Rust program implements the `World` trait (`init`/`update`/`view`, optional `layout`/`records`/`wants`/`snapshot`/`restore`) and `plaza_guest!` emits all 14 documented Plaza ABI v1 exports with the exact signatures from `examples/roc-world/ABI.md`: model as an opaque pointer, host inputs in `plaza_alloc` memory freed by `plaza_free`, one shared output slot, snapshot/restore as a total pair. Helper modules equal the Roc platform libraries: - `screen` = Screen.roc — cell grid, `boxed`, plain text, and the versioned screen JSON (the Roc `expect` values are reproduced byte-for-byte in tests) - `json` = RocJson.roc — bounded decode (64 KiB / depth 64), number lexemes preserved, first-key `get`, validating encode - `grid` = RocGrid.roc — total, bounds-checked row-major grids - `cap` = RocCap.roc — `r` request sessions, request-document builders, result routing - `text` = RocText.roc — total text helpers **`pkgs/id/examples/rust-counter` — the playable example.** Twin of `roc-counter`: trimmed `inc` increments, boxed 20x3 `count=N` screen, layout widening at 30 columns, `{"count":N}` records, `{}` wants, decimal snapshot with total restore. `build.sh` rebuilds the checked-in `counter.wasm` (`wasm32-unknown-unknown`); the module exports exactly `memory` + the 14 `plaza_*` functions and has no imports. **Conformance:** `rust-counter` joins `CONFORMANCE_MODULES` in `pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs`, so the F12.7 suite — documented export signatures vs ABI.md, ABI version 1, snapshot/restore byte-identical round-trip, records/wants schema validity — now exercises a Rust guest end to end. ## Verification (laptop) - `cargo test` in `rust-world`: 9 passed. In `rust-counter`: 2 passed. - `cargo test --lib sandbox::` in `pkgs/id`: 36 passed, including all five `conformance_*` tests with the rust-counter fixture. - PR checks were QUEUED at open time (fleet CI stall); merging under standing merge authority on this verification. ## Not in this slice The AssemblyScript-vs-Zig second SDK and the Wasm component-model/WIT direction — Drew-owned decisions recorded on #1065. issue.title: feat(id): F12.9 program upgrade with state migration and rollback (#1066)
issue.body: ## F12.9 program upgrade with state migration and rollback (#1066) Implements the confirmed F12.9 remainder for task 12962, now that the gate has landed: issue #1065 (F12.8 guest SDKs) closed via PR #7891 (merged 2026-11-09T01:03Z), verified fresh at claim time. Before this PR, `pkgs/id/src/world/` had no upgrade module, no migrate export, no versioned program-state snapshot format, and no upgrade runner. ### What lands New module `pkgs/id/src/world/upgrade.rs`, re-exported from `crate::world`: - **Versioned snapshot format for world program state** — `ProgramSnapshot` with a magic + format-version envelope. Format v1 (magic, one version byte, raw state) is still decoded so old snapshots upgrade; everything new is encoded at the current format v2 (version, state length, state, FNV-1a checksum), and the decoded snapshot records the format version it was read from. - **Optional `migrate` export in the guest ABI** — the `MigrateExport` host-side contract: `migrate(state, from_version, to_version) -> Result`. Programs without the export (`None`) keep working under the pre-existing behavior: their state is carried across the upgrade byte-for-byte. - **Probe-first upgrade runner** — `upgrade_program` decodes and migrates a probe copy of the state, re-encodes it at the current snapshot format, and reads it back; the running program's version and snapshot are swapped only if the migrated state round-trips exactly. Any failure (migrate refuses, migrated state over the 4 MiB bound, round-trip mismatch) leaves the old program bit-for-bit unchanged — that is the rollback. ### Exit tests (plan, Phase 12 F12.9) In-module tests, each naming its oracle: - `counter_upgrades_across_a_snapshot_format_change` — a v1 ASCII-decimal counter in a v1 snapshot upgrades to a v2 little-endian counter in a current-format snapshot, same value. - `failing_upgrade_leaves_the_old_program_running` — a deliberately failing `migrate` leaves version and snapshot bytes unchanged. - Plus: current-format round-trip records its version, legacy v1 snapshots still decode, corrupted snapshots are refused, no-`migrate` programs carry state unchanged, oversized migrated state rolls back. Targeted tests run on the laptop before opening (`cargo test --lib world::upgrade`: 7 passed); full verification is CI per fleet policy. ### Scope notes - No F12.8 work (issue #1065, landed separately) and no F12.15 work (issue #558, the downstream consumer of this migration path). - The runner is the transport-independent core seam (alongside the BUILDER-gated program install/upgrade path in `world/mod.rs`); wiring it into a live hot-swap command is follow-up work, not hidden in this PR. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

issue.title: feat(id): id world dev phase 1 — one-shot local compile + disposable scratch world (#5541)

labels.name: audit:completed-later
labels.description: Gap completed by later merged PR

issue.body: Implements **Phase 1** of the F12.15 `id world dev` authoring loop for #5541 (design: `doc/2026-11-01_design_id558.md`). The design's dependency gate is now satisfied — F12.9 #1066 landed via #8031 and F12.8 #1065 is closed — verified fresh this shift before starting. ## What this slice does - **`id world dev DIR`** (sandbox feature): source discovery for an app directory (`main.roc` first, sibling `.roc` files in name order, size-capped reads, validated by the compiler's own bounds), platform resolution from `main.roc`'s declared platform path (or `--platform`), and compilation through the existing bounded compiler engine (`world_compile::compile`). A local dev session grants every module its platform provides; hosted worlds keep their capability ceilings. - **Disposable scratch world**: the compiled module launches into an in-memory `WorldCore` + `WorldHandle` with a sandbox guest — the design's chosen local actor seam. No host is contacted, nothing is installed into a named world, and the scratch state is discarded when the session ends. - `--input TEXT` (repeatable) sends inputs as the dev guest; the command prints one JSON report: source files, seed, module size, compiler diagnostics, source-build provenance, initial view, view after each input, records sequence. ## Verification - `cargo test --lib -- world_dev test_cli_parse_world_dev` — **5 passed** on the laptop. The lifecycle test is the disposability oracle: the checked-in Roc counter starts at `count=0`, applies `inc` inputs through the actor to `count=2`, and a fresh launch starts again at `count=0`. - New module is `rustfmt`-clean; CLI parse test covers the new subcommand. ## Known gap (pre-existing, not this PR) An end-to-end compile of a Roc app cannot run on the laptop today: the platform host build (`examples/roc-world/build-host.sh`) fails on the installed Zig 0.17 (`Optimize.Debug` removed), so `targets/wasm32/host.wasm` cannot be produced. Filed as **#8152**. The compile leg here reuses `world_compile::compile`, which the host `Compile` path already exercises; once #8152 lands, `id world dev pkgs/id/examples/roc-counter --input inc` is the e2e check. ## Follow-ups (later design phases, staying on #5541) Watch/debounce + F12.9 hot-swap via `world::upgrade`, fixture promotion gates (dev-only cross-module-hash replay), deterministic fuzz + declared invariants, latency benchmark + authoring docs. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added `id world dev` for compiling and running an app locally in an offline, disposable environment. * Specify an app directory and optionally a platform, Roc compiler, seed, and ordered text inputs. * View the initial state and the result after each input in a JSON report.

First-pass research + design record for the Phase-14 Program ecosystem core topic: `doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/`.

- D1 program identity = (author public key, name, version, content hash); same-version/different-hash is a surfaced provenance violation
- D2 the signed bundle (per F12.17 #1069, ABI descriptor per F12.7 #1064) is the unit of travel; sideloading always works, fully offline
- D3 fork lineage is structural and cumulative in the bundle — attribution cannot be stripped without breaking provenance
- D4 install/update authority: pinned by default; updates beyond the F12.7/F12.9 no-approval envelope need explicit world-owner approval
- D5 template worlds strip members, credentials, per-user data, and grants by default, recorded in the template manifest
- D6 the gallery is a plural registry protocol (big server / pkarr / self-host, one record, over iroh); validity is protocol, admission is operator policy
- 7 invariants, 5 alternatives rejected, and the v1–v4 ladder (#6291, #6293, #6294, #6295) mapped; this record meets v1's entry condition

## Implementation issues filed from the record

- #8280 — signed program bundle format + sideload import
- #8281 — gallery registry protocol + reference registry service
- #8282 — template-world snapshot export/import

## Evidence

- Verification: `npx prettier --check` on the new doc + `doc/README.md` — pass; `git diff --check` — pass (docs-only change)
- Foundations re-verified fresh this shift: #1064, #1065, #1066, #1069, #1061 CLOSED; #6291/#6293/#6294/#6295 OPEN as the ladder; no pre-existing bundle/gallery/template implementation issues (GitHub search, 2026-11-10)

Closes #6278

issue.title: watchdog: reopen issues the bot wrongly closes on merges

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

issue.body:
## Problem in plain words

The developing-today[bot] status automation closes GitHub issues seconds after a PR merge that merely references them (Refs-only, no closing keyword) and labels them status:done — defect tracked in #7610. Until the integration rule is fixed at the source (ordered by Drew 2026-11-14), and as a permanent safety net afterwards, nothing watches for these wrongful closures: epic #9106 sat closed for ~14.75 hours (2026-11-12 21:04 CST to 2026-11-13 11:48 CST) before a person noticed, and epic #9078 had an elaboration task wrongly consumed as already_done because the epic looked done.

## What this builds

A closure watchdog polling recent issue-close events in developing-today/code (plus developing-today/opencode and developing-today/openchamber, covered by the same app installation) every 15 minutes. When an automation (in practice developing-today[bot]) closes an issue and either:

- (a) the issue has OPEN sub-issues (native sub-issues API), or
- (b) the closing PR referenced the issue WITHOUT a closing keyword (Closes/Fixes/Resolves #n) in its title/body — i.e. a Refs-only merge,

then the watchdog: reopens the issue, removes the status:done label, posts a short evidence comment (closing actor, close time, closing PR, which rule fired), and reports the reopen to the ID & Atlas Space owner chat.

Legitimate closes (closing keyword present, or a human close with no linked merged PR) are left untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Watchdog runs on a schedule of at most every 15-30 minutes and keeps a watermark so each close event is processed once.
- [x] Dry-run against the historical #9106 timeline (PR #9184 merged 2026-11-13T03:03:53Z, bot close 03:04:00Z, title reference only, open sub-issues) shows it would have fired both rules.
- [x] Dry-run against the #9078 closure pattern shows rule (a) firing (closed with open components).
- [ ] A live wrongful close (or the verification fixture from #7610) is reopened with status:done stripped and an evidence comment posted.
- [x] No legitimate Closes-keyword close is reopened in dry-run or live operation.

Filed 2026-11-14 under Drew's direct order to fix #7610 and implement this watchdog.

issue.body:
Sibling of #7016 (which covers open-issue↔queue coverage and the done-task-only class). This issue governs the mirror audit Drew ordered 2026-11-07 20:40 CST after the 766 verification found only 8 of 766 "done" tasks were truly done: **double-check every closed issue and PR, and verify each unmerged branch with commits and unpushed worktrees.**

## First-tranche results (2026-11-07 evening, read-only audit)

Evidence file: `~/workspace/scratch/closure-audit-2026-11-07.md` (fleet-local).

**Part 1 — closed issues.** Totals: code 2,612 closed issues / opencode 939 / openchamber 845 / darwin-nix 840 (5,236). Verified the 200 most-recently-closed per repo tranche (darwin 60, openchamber 60, opencode 40, code 40) at the 766's evidence standard:
- 183/200 (91.5%) LEGITIMATE-LINKED (merged PR or closing commit on the timeline).
- 10/200 NO-EVIDENCE by linkage — all 10 read individually: **10/10 legitimate-by-record** (the closure evidence lives in agent-note comments: done-notes citing merge commits, supersession records, decommission records). Confirmed wrongful closures in the tranche: **0**.
- 7/200 DISPOSITION (not_planned/duplicate — incl. 4 "Scheduled Bolt" bot issues).
- Merged-PR "Fixes #N" spot check: 12/12 claimed targets actually closed, no negation traps.
- Closed-unmerged PRs: 326 total (code 206, darwin 55, opencode 39, openchamber 26). Sample of 12 most-recent per repo set: **12/12 closed as superseded/duplicate with a salvage note naming the canonical merged PR.** Zero silently abandoned in sample.

Methodological finding: linkage-only verification UNDERCOUNTS legitimacy — fleet closures carry their evidence in comments, not GitHub linkage. Remainder verification must read the record, not just the timeline.

**Part 2 — unmerged branches.** Remote branches: code 1,702 / opencode 322 / openchamber 221 / darwin 46. From the laptop primaries post-fetch, remote-tracking branches not merged into main: **196, all of them `archive/janitor-2026-11-07/*`** (the disk janitor's by-design archives; 0 non-archive). Local unmerged branches: nix 31 non-archive (mostly `queue/*` task branches, Nov 2–4), opencode ≥48 non-archive, code primaries hit the 100-branch listing cap with archives — full local census remains. Local "unmerged" overstates stranding (squash/merge-commit landings leave local branches permanently unmerged by SHA); patch-equivalence review is the real test.

**Part 3 — worktrees.** Laptop: 67 clone/worktree dirs scanned at ~/git top level + primaries. Named substantive holds:
- `~/git/wt-atlas-snowflake-swap` (feat/atlas-snowflake-production): 6,120 commits not in fork main; `~/git/wt-atlas-vector-backend`: 6,221 — divergent Atlas lineage, needs equivalence review, not assumed stranded.
- `~/git/fleet` (fleet repo clone): **1,556 dirty files** on main, no origin/main tracking ref — biggest single uncommitted pile.
- Small not-in-main commit counts (1–2) on ~10 queue worktrees, incl. `wt-id806` (design/id-806, #806 design work, Nov 1) and `devtoday-openchamber` queue/8357-224 (stale since Oct 22).
- Sandbox: no unpushed commits anywhere; one pushed-but-unmerged branch `docs/id-roadmap-phase14` (ID roadmap Phase 14 plan of record, epic #6312) in ~/git/devtoday-code; hatch-personal measured 0 ahead / 0 behind at 2026-11-08T02:52Z, contradicting Lane 4's 17:48 measurement of 244/45 — re-verify.

## Remainder (enqueued as queue tasks under this issue)
- Per-repo verification of the remaining ~5,036 closed issues (read-the-record standard; batched tranches of ~200).
- Full closed-unmerged PR verification (326).
- Local-branch full census without listing caps + patch-equivalence review for the stranded candidates; Atlas worktree equivalence; ~/git/fleet dirty-pile disposition review; hatch-personal divergence re-measurement.

Doctrine (Drew, 2026-11-07): triage completion never counts as done; this audit's tasks complete only with per-item evidence recorded.


## Acceptance criteria
- The problem described above is confirmed against current main (reproduced or traced to the named code path), or the issue is closed with that evidence.
- A fix/implementation addressing the described behaviour is merged via PR referencing this issue, with tests naming their oracle where the change has meaningful invariants.
- Related/sibling issues from the same filing batch are cross-linked and any dependency is recorded as a native blocked-by relation.

issue.body:
## What and why

Follow-on to #788 (F13.6), split out by the Q1 decision recorded on #788 on 2026-11-22: F13.6's first shell is contract-parity only, so the rich native surfaces its motivation names (3D, audio, native widgets) live here instead. Today's typed presentation has exactly one variant, `WorldSurface::Screen`; richer semantics cannot be claimed by a shell that only implements the screen/text view — they need a separately designed, versioned, host-validated presentation extension first (design of record: `doc/2026-11-01_design_id788.md` §7 steps 3–4, §6 conditional criteria).

## Scope — two steps, in order, separate PRs

1. **Portable rich-presentation contract.** Design and validate the minimal typed scene/audio/widget payloads in the existing optional `surface` slot of the server `view` (or propose a separately versioned alternative if that slot cannot express them). Update host validation, the machine-readable contract (`pkgs/id/contract/shell-contract.v1.json`), and conformance/fallback tests in its own PR. Any new frame kind waits for the F11.12 gate — prefer the `surface` slot, which needs none.
2. **Bevy rich-surface renderers.** Add renderers and a deterministic example world for only the payloads accepted in step 1, in `pkgs/id/crates/id-native-shell`; world input stays on the same contract frames.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The selected surface schema has explicit versions, bounds, safe fallback behavior, contract/conformance coverage, and host-side validation before the Bevy renderer consumes it
- [ ] Old shells still render `view.data` unchanged; malformed or oversized rich surfaces are refused by host validation
- [ ] A real session demonstrates each selected surface in the native shell, its transcript passes `id world contract --check`, and an older shell's text fallback remains usable
- [ ] No WIT/component-model dependency: per the #788 decision record, WIT (F12.8/#1065) governs the guest ABI only and does not change the shell contract

## Prerequisites

- #788 (F13.6) — closed complete 2026-11-22; its Bevy reference shell and the F13.1 conformance seam are the foundation here
- F11.12 journal/frame gating, only if a new frame kind is proposed

## Size

XL (two sequenced steps; step 1 is the design-bearing one)

# LANE 4 — MERGED-PR-AUDIT — AUDIT-7 tracking

Umbrella: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13871

Scope: every PR merged since 2026-10-23 across:
- developing-today/code
- developing-today-forks/opencode
- developing-today-forks/openchamber
- dezren39/fleet

Method: one by one, read PR + diff in full; compare to spawning issue (especially Closes/fixes); check later PRs completed earlier gaps before filing; file real gaps/bugs/next-steps properly prioritised; apply documented outcome labels; per-PR ledger in final report.

Outcome labels (Lane 4 set, documented here and in final report):
- `audit:complete` — PR fully implemented its spawning issue / stated intent, no gap found
- `audit:partial` — PR partially implemented; gap filed (linked in ledger/comment)
- `audit:gap-filed` — a gap / unfiled next step was filed as a new issue from this PR
- `audit:bug-filed` — a bug found in the merged diff was filed as a new issue
- `audit:completed-later` — earlier gap was completed by a later merged PR (linked)
- `audit:no-issue` — PR had no spawning issue to compare against (verdict on stated intent only)

Progress will be posted at every slice boundary (per repo / per batch).

Status: STARTED 2026-11-23 — enumerating merged PRs since 2026-10-23.
